props.title: Five formats for your corporate event

rows.text: Booking from late November into January, the holiday party is something special for your employees and associates.
An evening built around your programming (likely including remarks, an auction, videos and walks to the stage). We work together on cues so the music flows seamlessly with the night.

Dinners where the conversation is the event. Many times we recommend a jazz duo playing low enough to add a sense of class to the ambience without demanding attention away from developing relationships.
Retreats and incentive trips in the mountain corridor, Vail through Aspen, and the Colorado foothills. We create the evening to meet the expectations of a group that flew in for it.

You know your people better than we do - and some people like to keep going after the first party ends. The hour after a conference dinner, a gala program or the holiday party’s speeches, with a DJ alone (or a DJ plus a live musician over top), a band that lets the crowd sing, or live band karaoke.

props.html: A jazz band across the whole evening, from the moment the doors open to the after-party, is on the corporate jazz band page. What each size costs in this market is in the cost guide. Want some more ideas? Check out our thoughts on the whole evening in corporate event entertainment ideas in Denver. More ideas for a fundraiser or an award night are in gala dinner entertainment ideas. Even more out of the box: you can book a seventy-five-minute corporate sound bath for a wellness week, an offsite or a transition day, with the whole team enjoying some deep, meditative rest. Find out more on the daytime sound bath page. A retirement party the company throws is one of the things we would love to help you spoil a VIP with.

props.html: Mountain venues run on their own rules, and where there’s a sound cap we want the number in the contract: a band that knows the limit in advance chooses arrangements and instrumentation that stay inside it, which sounds better than a band turning down. Every town’s cap, cited and dated, is on the mountain page.
We settle setup with the venue before the day, from dock times to where the cases sit during dinner, and all of it is written down by band size.
Travel is its own line on the quote, and so is a night’s lodging past the passes. The retreats page covers the resort towns one by one.

props.html: We Work around your event's program

Every great corporate evening runs on great programming. You've got remarks from leadership, maybe an an award or auction, a window of time where people need to hear each other talk. Dinner and networking are served with live music at conversation volume, and the night can get loud later, when loud is exactly the point.
The music stops while your CEO is still three steps from the microphone. Transitions are planned with the run of show.

We work awards dinners, auctions, remarks and a video the same way: music up to the moment, silence through it, music again when the applause starts. If the program wants a louder set, live band karaoke is its own act: the band plays the hits on its own and hands the mic to whoever wants a song.

Galas and fundraisers book this way too, at the same sizes. A reception set plays through arrival, dinner music runs around the program, and the auction, the paddle raise and the thank-yous are treated as cues the band works around. The galas and award nights page covers every cue.

items.q: What does live music cost for a corporate event in Denver?
items.a: It depends on the size of the act, the hours it plays and the date. We don't publish prices, because one figure would be wrong for most of the nights somebody read it on. What live music costs across this market is on our pricing page, with its sources. Send the date, the venue and the guest count and you get our number for that night.

items.q: How far in advance should we book?
items.a: Corporate holiday parties are typically decided August through October for November and December dates, and New Year's Eve books earliest of all. Client dinners and retreats run on shorter windows, and any date gets a straight yes or no by email.

items.q: Can you work with our procurement process?
items.a: Yes. We can be set up as a vendor, quote against a purchase order, and invoice net-30 on approval. A certificate of insurance naming your venue, a W-9 and one itemized invoice, with everything on separate lines, arrive in the same email as the contract. Vendor onboarding is usually the slowest step, so start it early.

items.q: How loud is the band during dinner and networking?
items.a: Quiet enough to talk across without raising your voice, about 60 to 65 dBA at the nearest table for a planner who wants the number. The dance floor later in the night runs around 88 to 95 dBA, when loud is the point. If your venue enforces a cap, give us the number when we sign and the night is built under it.
